title: Tenant-aware billing offsets adjudication worker for late-arrival usage
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Summary: Implement a resilient, tenant-aware background worker that adjudicates billing offsets when usage events arrive out-of-order or after billing windows close. This job will compute adjustments (credits/debits) and emit stable ledger entries with provenance tags.

Scope:
- Ingest late-arrival usage records from the usage-events S3 topic and changefeed.
- Group by tenant -> billing window -> route/model and compute net offset against already-finalized windows.
- Apply deduplication heuristics (session fingerprint + event-hash + ingest-timestamp tolerance).
- Emit immutable offset records to the billing-ledger topic and push a compensated journal to the billing-cdc for downstream invoicing.
- Record audit metadata for each adjustment: source_event_ids, adjudication_reason, confidence_score, operator_id (system), and link to debug traces.

Goals & acceptance criteria:
- Latency: reconciliation worker processes backlog at >= 10k events/min on m4-worker cluster for typical customers.
- Accuracy: >99.95% dedupe precision on synthetic fuzz tests; sampled production checks show <0.1% incorrect adjustments.
- Traceability: each emitted ledger entry must include provenance and a linkable trace id.
- Safety: job must never shrink a finalized invoice without an authorized admin rollback path; offsets are issued as compensated line items.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We select an append-only compensated-offset model rather than mutating historic invoice rows to preserve auditable history and enable deterministic reruns. Trade-off: customers will see separate offset line items instead of retroactive invoice edits which simplifies audits but requires clearer UI treatment in Console.
- Use an idempotent adjudication key (tenant|window_start|route|event_hash) to avoid double-crediting; store adjudication keys in a compact RocksDB per-partition index to minimize remote lookups. This increases memory per worker but reduces cross-service coordination.
- Conservative dedupe window: 72 hours by default with tenant-configurable TTL. Shorter windows for low-latency customers might increase risk of duplicates.

Data contract & outputs:
- Input: raw_usage_events topic schema (event_id, tenant_id, route, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, ingest_ts, source, signature).
- Output ledger record: {ledger_id, tenant_id, window_start, offset_amount, unit, adjudication_key, reason, source_event_ids[], created_at, trace_url}. (Stored as JSON in billing-ledger topic). Note: in practice this schema is documented in Confluence link below.

Operational runbook & monitoring:
- Dashboards: backlog size, processed events/min, average adjudication latency, offset_amount histogram, error-rate per-tenant.
- Alerts: backlog > 6 hours for >= 5% of tenants; duplicate-offset detection spike > 0.5% of operations; RocksDB OOM events.
- Rollout plan: start with 10 small tenants on canary run for two days, then 100 tenants for one week, then full rollout with throttled concurrency.

References & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Redwood/Billing+Offsets+Adjudication (internal)
- Spike PR with benchmark harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/412
- Dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/usage/billing-offsets
- Example compensated ledger record (playbook): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/offsets-playbook

Risks:
- Misclassification of duplicate events could cause overstated credits — mitigated by sampling, canary, and manual review flows.
- RocksDB growth on hot tenants — mitigate with eviction and tombstone compaction job.
- Legal/invoice expectations: accounting team prefers mutating invoices for small enterprise customers; we'll coordinate with finance to represent offsets clearly in customer statements.
